title: configureApplication
summary: Configure URL handling and consumer-owned route presentation for React or Preact.

sections.title: Parameters
sections.body: Accepts one ApplicationEnvironment object. Fields may be omitted. resolveURL maps a destination before application navigation; isDocumentHandoff selects document links for a custom handoff; leaveDocument performs external navigation; entryScript supplies the source rendered by Scripts.

sections.title: Returns and lifetime
sections.body: Returns void. Each call replaces the entire configuration rather than merging fields. Call configureApplication({}) to restore defaults. The configuration is module-scoped, so do not set request-specific server data here.

sections.title: Usage
sections.body: Configure only the deployment behavior your application needs, then mount it. The route list remains the source of route matching and loader/action registration.

sections.title: Navigation and scripts
sections.body: Without leaveDocument, a selected handoff uses location.assign. A custom leaveDocument callback must carry out navigation itself. Modified clicks, download links, and non-self targets retain browser behavior. entryScript is trusted executable source rendered by Scripts; it is not escaped as text or loaded as a URL.

sections.title: Consumer-owned route commits
sections.body: commitRoute(commit, previous, next) receives the previous and next route snapshots and a synchronous DOM commit function. Without it, Smolter commits immediately. It applies to mountApplication and nested routers in both adapters, not a bare routing-only store. Initial loading, errors, and same-URL revalidation can also commit: the consumer chooses which updates to animate. Smolter does not call startViewTransition, inspect reduced-motion settings, compare components, or choose CSS/duration. Call commit once; callbacks superseded by newer work or disposal do nothing. The callback return value is not awaited. If you defer the call, you own completing it and handling your animation promises/errors. Recovery still owns withholding obsolete errors. Configuration is application-wide, not per navigation.
